title: Great Britain and England 1660-1780: population, real GDP per head, nominal GDP and the national debt (annual)
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheet 'A2. Pop of Eng & GB 1086-1870' (Broadberry, Campbell, Klein, Overton and van Leeuwen 2015), sheet 'A21. GDP per capita 1086+' (England: Broadberry et al. 2015; Great Britain from 1700) and sheet 'A29. The National Debt' (Mitchell 1988; capital value of terminable annuities from Parliamentary Papers 1898)
series: A2: 'Population of England, millions' (pop_england_m). A21, block 'England': 'Real GDP per capita' at 2013 market prices, £ (england_real_gdp_pc_2013gbp); block 'Great Britain', from 1700: 'Nominal GDP' (gb_nominal_gdp_gbp_m, £ m), 'Population' (pop_gb_m, millions) and 'Real GDP per capita' at 2013 prices, £ (gb_real_gdp_pc_2013gbp). A29, par values at the end of the financial year, £ m: 'Total funded and unfunded debt of the UK' (total_debt_gbp_m, from 1690), the spliced total including the estimated capital value of terminable annuities (debt_incl_annuities_gbp_m) and that total as a per cent of nominal GDP (debt_pct_gdp, from 1699)
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources ('When using this data, please cite this source.', sheet A2, for Broadberry et al. 2015). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset (121 years, 8 columns) is stored here for teaching, with attribution.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb (the copy used for boe_millennium_england_debt). Sheet A21 states: 'NB The population series quoted here for GB uses those of Broadberry et al. (2015) rather than the alternative bottom up measures in the population sheet'. The populations are annual values interpolated between benchmark estimates, and real GDP per head is an annual reconstruction from output series: the chapter compares levels over decades (doubling times of population; the change of GDP per head from 1700 to 1776) and does not read year-to-year changes. The debt is at par (nominal) value; terminable annuities are outside the total and inside the spliced measure. The chapter compares Smith's 'more than £145,000,000 of debt' contracted in the four French wars (smith_facts, row wn_145) with the total at the end of the Seven Years' War (1763: 134.2; spliced 144.2) and gives the ratio to GDP in 1763 (118.1 per cent) and 1776 (97.5 per cent).
citation: Broadberry, S., B. M. S. Campbell, A. Klein, M. Overton and B. van Leeuwen (2015), British Economic Growth, 1270-1870, Cambridge University Press; Mitchell, B. R. (1988), British Historical Statistics, Cambridge University Press; data via Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017)
